sources.title: Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis: Biliary Ducts

records.name: Right hepatic duct
records.summary: The right hepatic duct collects bile from the right functional liver and ordinarily joins the left hepatic duct to form the common hepatic duct.
records.definition: An extrahepatic continuation of intrahepatic bile drainage from the right liver. Its contributing anterior and posterior sectoral ducts vary in branching and junction pattern.
records.function: Conveys bile toward the common hepatic duct.
relationships: Typically formed by right anterior and posterior hepatic sectoral ducts
Ordinarily joins the left hepatic duct at the hepatic duct confluence
records.clinical: Biliary branching variants are important in liver surgery, transplantation and biliary drainage.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Left hepatic duct
records.summary: The left hepatic duct carries bile drained from the left functional liver toward the confluence with the right hepatic duct.
records.definition: Collecting duct of the left functional liver, receiving tributaries from left hepatic segments and sometimes the caudate lobe.
records.function: Transports bile out of the left liver.
relationships: Receives segmental biliary tributaries
Ordinarily unites with the right hepatic duct to form the common hepatic duct
records.clinical: Variation in drainage patterns matters for biliary reconstruction and hepatic resection.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Common hepatic duct
records.summary: The common hepatic duct carries bile from the hepatic duct confluence toward its junction with the cystic duct.
records.definition: A segment of the extrahepatic biliary tract extending from the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts to the junction with the cystic duct.
records.function: Conducts hepatic bile toward the common bile duct or, via the cystic duct, the gallbladder.
relationships: Continues from the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts
Meets the cystic duct to form the common bile duct
records.clinical: An important landmark during biliary surgery; its position and branching may vary.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Gallbladder
records.summary: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile between meals and releases it into the biliary tract during digestion.
records.definition: A hollow, muscular organ on the visceral surface of the liver connected to the extrahepatic biliary tree through the cystic duct.
records.function: Stores and concentrates bile; contracts in response to feeding, particularly via cholecystokinin.
relationships: Lies against the inferior surface of the liver
Communicates with the common bile duct through the cystic duct
records.bloodSupply: Cystic artery, usually from the right hepatic artery.
records.innervation: Autonomic fibers through the hepatic plexus; sensory pathways contribute to referred pain.
records.development: Develops from the hepatic diverticulum of the embryonic foregut.
records.clinical: Gallstones may obstruct the cystic duct or migrate into the common bile duct.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Stomach
records.summary: The stomach stores food, mixes it with gastric secretions, and regulates delivery of chyme into the duodenum.
records.definition: An expandable muscular segment of the alimentary canal between the esophagus and duodenum, organized into cardia, fundus, body and pyloric region.
records.function: Mechanical mixing, acid and enzyme secretion, intrinsic factor production, and controlled gastric emptying.
relationships: Continuous with the esophagus proximally and duodenum distally
Located mainly in the epigastric and left upper abdominal regions
records.bloodSupply: Branches of the celiac trunk via the gastric, gastro-omental and short gastric arteries.
records.innervation: Vagal parasympathetic fibers and sympathetic fibers primarily through the celiac plexus.
records.development: Forms through expansion and rotation of the embryonic foregut.
records.clinical: Peptic ulcer disease can affect the gastric mucosa and may cause bleeding or perforation.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Pancreas
records.summary: The pancreas produces digestive enzymes and bicarbonate for the duodenum and releases hormones that regulate blood glucose.
records.definition: An elongated, predominantly retroperitoneal gland extending from the duodenal C-loop toward the splenic hilum, with exocrine and endocrine components.
records.function: Exocrine secretion of digestive enzymes and bicarbonate; endocrine secretion including insulin and glucagon.
relationships: Its head lies within the curve of the duodenum
Its tail approaches the splenic hilum
records.bloodSupply: Pancreaticoduodenal arcades and branches of the splenic artery.
records.innervation: Autonomic fibers reaching the organ through celiac and superior mesenteric plexuses.
records.development: Arises from dorsal and ventral endodermal pancreatic buds that fuse.
records.clinical: Pancreatitis, duct obstruction, and pancreatic tumors may affect adjacent biliary structures.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Duodenum
records.summary: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine, receiving gastric contents, bile, and pancreatic secretions.
records.definition: A C-shaped segment of small intestine between the stomach and jejunum, divided into superior, descending, horizontal and ascending parts.
records.function: Neutralizes gastric acid and participates in digestion and nutrient absorption.
relationships: Surrounds the head of the pancreas
Receives biliary and pancreatic secretions at the major duodenal papilla in typical anatomy
records.innervation: Autonomic fibers via the celiac and superior mesenteric plexuses.
records.development: Develops from the terminal foregut and proximal midgut.
records.clinical: Duodenal ulcers and obstruction can affect this segment.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Trachea
records.summary: The trachea is the cartilage-supported airway connecting the larynx to the main bronchi.
records.definition: A flexible airway reinforced by C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings and lined by respiratory mucosa.
records.function: Conducts, warms and helps clear inspired air.
relationships: Begins inferior to the cricoid cartilage
Bifurcates at the carina into right and left main bronchi
records.bloodSupply: Regional branches including inferior thyroid and bronchial arteries.
records.innervation: Autonomic innervation with vagal parasympathetic input.
records.development: Forms from the ventral laryngotracheal diverticulum of the foregut.
records.clinical: Endotracheal intubation and tracheostomy require knowledge of its position and neighboring structures.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Diaphragm
records.summary: The diaphragm is the principal muscle of inspiration, separating the thoracic cavity from the abdomen.
records.definition: A dome-shaped musculotendinous partition with sternal, costal and lumbar attachments converging on a central tendon.
records.function: Contraction lowers the diaphragm and increases thoracic volume during inspiration.
records.origin: Xiphoid process, inferior six costal cartilages and adjacent ribs, and lumbar crura and arcuate ligaments.
records.bloodSupply: Pericardiacophrenic, musculophrenic, superior phrenic and inferior phrenic arteries.
relationships: Separates thorax and abdomen
Contains caval, esophageal and aortic passageways
records.development: Forms from septum transversum, pleuroperitoneal membranes, dorsal mesentery of esophagus and body wall.
records.clinical: Phrenic nerve injury may impair ventilation and produce hemidiaphragm elevation.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Right rectus femoris
records.summary: The right rectus femoris crosses the hip and knee, flexing the hip and extending the knee.
records.definition: A bipennate muscle of the anterior thigh and one of the four quadriceps femoris components.
records.function: Extends the knee and assists hip flexion.
records.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine (straight head) and ilium superior to the acetabulum (reflected head).
records.insertion: Patella via quadriceps tendon and tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament.
records.bloodSupply: Predominantly lateral circumflex femoral artery branches.
relationships: Superficial to vastus intermedius
Part of the quadriceps extensor mechanism
records.development: Differentiates from embryonic limb-bud muscle precursors.
records.clinical: May be strained during sprinting or kicking; avulsion can occur at the anterior inferior iliac spine.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.

records.name: Left rectus femoris
records.summary: The left rectus femoris crosses the hip and knee, flexing the hip and extending the knee.
records.definition: A bipennate muscle of the anterior thigh and one of the four quadriceps femoris components.
records.function: Extends the knee and assists hip flexion.
records.origin: Anterior inferior iliac spine (straight head) and ilium superior to the acetabulum (reflected head).
records.insertion: Patella via quadriceps tendon and tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament.
records.bloodSupply: Predominantly lateral circumflex femoral artery branches.
relationships: Superficial to vastus intermedius
Part of the quadriceps extensor mechanism
records.development: Differentiates from embryonic limb-bud muscle precursors.
records.clinical: May be strained during sprinting or kicking; avulsion can occur at the anterior inferior iliac spine.
records.note: Editorial educational synthesis; terminology and detailed clinical fields require individual expert review.
